newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. wants to ease school bond requirements.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. wants to ease school bond requirements.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson will seek an amendment to the state constitution to allow local school bond measures to pass with a simple majority of votes instead of a two-thirds majority, a spokeswoman said on Friday.
The change is one of the reforms Wilson is proposing to the school construction process, his office said. Wilson will detail the reforms in his annual State of the State speech next Tuesday.

Most local school bond measures must be approved by voters, often by a two-thirds majority. Wilson will seek a constitutional amendment to reduce the number of votes required to pass a local school bond issue to a simple majority, Wilson spokeswoman Lisa Kalustian said.
Wilson's reforms would also require that the state fund no more than half of needed school construction costs.

Wilson spokesman Sean Walsh told reporters on Friday that he expected there would be "some tax cut component" in Wilson's proposed state budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting July 1. He gave no details.
The Republican governor will announce his budget plans next week.
Wilson's proposal for a 15 percent state income tax cut was defeated in the state legislature last year.
Wilson also said on Friday that his proposed budget will provide an additional $57.5 million to help improve reading instruction in California schools.
